applies_why: The judge makes the almah/bethulah word-count cutting both ways a reason for UNDERDETERMINED, treating a dual-sense matter as open.
quote: the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8)
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: The phrase 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand': I weighed whether it forbids using dual-sense/word-count ambivalence as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED, versus reading it only as a rule that both senses count and does not address word studies.
why: Because the judge cites the word-count cutting both ways as part of the UNDERDETERMINED result, it treats a dual-sense matter as open, which K-S2 forbids.
